soil-fert-244.q: Why do dairy and beef manures influence organic matter more than poultry or swine manure?
soil-fert-244.a: They hold undigested forage and bedding rich in lignin.

soil-fert-251.q: What happens to fall-applied manure in humid climates?
soil-fert-251.a: Ammonium converts to nitrate that leaches or denitrifies; a New York study found about twice the N leaching from fall as from spring application.

soil-water-091.q: What happens to soil under buildings and roads?
soil-water-091.a: It is sealed off from rainfall and the nutrient cycle, so it is in effect consumed and made infertile.

soil-water-022.q: What does impervious surface do to groundwater and flooding?
soil-water-022.a: Less water reaches groundwater, so the water table falls and droughts worsen, while more water left on the surface causes flooding.

soil-water-103.q: Why can gelifluction occur on slopes of less than half a degree?
soil-water-103.a: The waterlogged topsoil flows like a liquid.

soil-water-251.q: Which particles are held up by turbulence and travel in suspension?
soil-water-251.a: Particles of about 70 micrometres or less in air.

soil-water-067.q: In which four main ways do plants act on slopes?
soil-water-067.a: Wind throw, removal of water, the added mass of the vegetation (surcharge) and mechanical reinforcement by roots.

soil-water-300.q: What happens to quick clays when saturated?
soil-water-300.a: They liquefy and flow, causing mass wasting.

soil-agri-001.q: Before pedology arose in the 19th century, what was the only branch of soil science?

soil-agri-044.q: What does fallowing do for land and for pests?
soil-agri-044.a: It lets land recover and store organic matter while keeping moisture, and breaks pest and soil-borne pathogen cycles by removing their hosts.

soil-agri-042.q: What did a 2020 review of 229 articles find about the definition of regenerative agriculture?
soil-agri-042.a: No legal or widely accepted definition: some stress practices, others outcomes.

soil-agri-133.q: Why is crop rotation not intercropping?
soil-agri-133.a: Its crops grow in separate seasons.

soil-agri-034.q: What temperature must soil reach in solarization, and to what depth do pathogens die?
soil-agri-034.a: 35-60 °C, which kills pathogens in the top 30 cm.

soil-agri-138.q: Who is called the father of the Green Revolution, and what prize did he receive?
soil-agri-138.a: Norman Borlaug, who received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1970.

soil-agri-139.q: How much does 1 kg of dry coco peat expand to when moist?
soil-agri-139.a: 15 litres, with a pH of 5.5 to 6.5.

soil-agri-012.q: What do permanent indicators and point indicators describe?
soil-agri-012.a: Permanent indicators, chiefly soil properties, describe a field's main constants; point indicators track crop status such as disease, water stress or nitrogen stress.

soil-agri-039.q: How long can rock powder supply nutrients?
soil-agri-039.a: Up to 5 years: plants take what they need and the rest stays crystallized.

soil-agri-045.q: What should susceptible crops such as corn follow, rather than a fallow?
soil-agri-045.a: A cover crop that hosts the fungi, such as oats or another small grain.

soil-agri-148.a: No tillage, no fertilizer, no pesticides or herbicides, no weeding and no pruning.

soil-agri-179.a: By blowing air or steam through molten rock at about 1600 C, giving fine intertwined fibres 2 to 6 micrometres across.

soil-agri-182.q: Why do grass cover crops scavenge nitrogen and reduce erosion?
soil-agri-182.a: Their fibrous root systems scavenge leftover nutrients, especially nitrogen, and some establish rapidly.

soil-agri-198.q: What should follow a legume forage in rotation?
soil-agri-198.a: A high-nitrogen crop such as corn.

soil-agri-190.q: How do cover crops raise infiltration and water-holding capacity?
soil-agri-190.a: Infiltration through macropores, and water-holding capacity through organic matter; residue also slows runoff.

soil-agri-191.q: Are grain crops hosts of root-knot nematode?
soil-agri-191.a: No, they are nonhosts, so growing grains reduces numbers; very bad infestations may need two full grain seasons.

soil-agri-197.q: How long a break do diseases need from their host crops?
soil-agri-197.a: Some need only a one-year break; others need several years of nonhost crops to cut inoculum.

soil-agri-203.q: What is considered the foundation of modern agroecology?

soil-agri-223.q: What did centuries of tillage cause, especially around the Mediterranean?
soil-agri-223.a: Excessive erosion, organic matter loss and nutrient depletion.
